messages.subject: different parameter estimations
parts:
Hi all, 
I am curious as to why I am getting different parameter estimations using the mirt package from the ltm package when fitting a unidimensional 2PL. Can anyone explain as to how ltm is fitting vs mirt? Lmk if you'd like to see my code, or if I should clarify. thanks!
-Sebastian

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: different parameter estimations
parts:
ltm reports the classical IRT parameterization by default; mirt uses the slope-intercept form. Both packages can be changed though (mirt post-estimation, ltm within the ltm() function).

library(mirt)

dat <- expand.table(LSAT7)
mod <- mirt(dat, 1, '2PL')
coef(mod, simplify=TRUE)
coef(mod, simplify=TRUE, IRTpars=TRUE)

library(ltm)
ltm(dat ~ z1)
ltm(dat ~ z1, IRT.param = FALSE)

Phil
